description:
Geng-geng , a colloquial slang derived from 'gang,' refers to a modern Gen Z youth subculture that emerged in BGC (Bonifacio Global City), from Taguig, Philippines. They have gained prominence for having their self-proclaimed gangster individuals behave disruptively and rebelliously, as well as walking jointly in urban areas of the country with similar wardrobes to show solid collaboration and coolness. It became a platform for young Filipinos as an opportunity to escape from strict, unexceptional standards from older generations. [ 1 ]

While the style was generally characterized as " Y2K -inspired streetwear," it made a bold juxtaposition of Avant-garde (long, layered skirts worn by male counterparts, pioneered by a social media personality, Kiel the Great) while keeping it straightforward with a clear Hypebeast influence at times, creating a unique, contemporary fashion identity.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Tough attitude
